description:
This file is a shell script designed to generate QoS (Quality of Service) configurations for OpenWRT networking devices. It includes functionalities for adding modules, parsing network configurations, setting up traffic control (tc) rules, managing firewall rules, and configuring network interfaces for QoS.

The script interacts with external configuration tools and system utilities such as iptables, tc, and modules, emphasizing its role in network configuration automation within an OpenWRT environment.

methods.name: add_insmod
methods.description: Adds a kernel module if not already loaded, using modprobe or insmod depending on system availability.

methods.name: find_ifname
methods.description: Determines the network device name for a given interface, using network_get_device if network config exists.

methods.name: parse_matching_rule
methods.description: Parses traffic matching rules and constructs iptables rules with various options like protocol, ports, source/destination addresses, DSCP, TOS, etc.

methods.name: config_cb
methods.description: Handles configuration parsing for network interfaces and classification rules.

methods.name: qos_parse_config
methods.description: Parses individual QoS configuration sections and sets up interface classes and classification rules.

methods.name: enum_classes
methods.description: Enumerates and assigns class numbers to QoS classes.

methods.name: tcrules
methods.description: Generates traffic control rules via an awk script, possibly for shaping traffic.

methods.name: start_interface
methods.description: Initializes QoS settings for a specific network interface, including traffic control and firewall rules.

methods.name: start_interfaces
methods.description: Iterates over all configured interfaces to initialize QoS settings.

methods.name: add_rules
methods.description: Adds iptables rules for QoS classification and marking.

methods.name: start_cg
methods.description: Starts a QoS class group, setting up iptables rules and traffic shape configurations for it.

methods.name: start_firewall
methods.description: Initializes firewall rules related to QoS, including module loading and chain setup.

methods.name: stop_firewall
methods.description: Removes QoS-related iptables rules and chains to clean up QoS configurations.
